questions.prompt: The base of a right-angled triangle is 15 cm and its hypotenuse is 25 cm. Find its area.
questions.answer:
1. Find altitude h by Pythagoras theorem:
h = √(252 - 152) = √(625 - 225) = √400 = 20 cm.

2. Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 15 × 20 = 150 cm2.
questions.markingScheme:
• Altitude h = 20 cm: 1 mark
• Area = 150 cm2: 1 mark

questions.prompt: If 2<sup>x</sup> = 3<sup>y</sup> = 6<sup>-z</sup>, prove that: 1/x + 1/y + 1/z = 0.
questions.answer:
Let 2x = 3y = 6-z = k.
Then: 2 = k1/x, 3 = k1/y, and 6 = k-1/z.

We know that: 2 × 3 = 6.
Substitute the values of 2, 3, and 6 in terms of k:
k1/x × k1/y = k-1/z
k(1/x + 1/y) = k-1/z.

Equating exponents:
1/x + 1/y = -1/z
⇒ 1/x + 1/y + 1/z = 0. (Hence Proved).
questions.markingScheme:
• Setting terms equal to k and expressing 2, 3, 6 in powers of k: 1 mark
• Using 2 × 3 = 6: 1 mark
• Equating exponents to conclude proof: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Classic high-order thinking skills (HOTS) exponent problem.

questions.prompt: Factorize: x<sup>3</sup> + 13x<sup>2</sup> + 32x + 20.
questions.answer:
Let p(x) = x3 + 13x2 + 32x + 20.
Factors of 20: ±1, ±2, ±4, ±5, ±10.
Test x = -1: p(-1) = (-1)3 + 13(-1)2 + 32(-1) + 20 = -1 + 13 - 32 + 20 = 0.
⇒ (x + 1) is a factor.

Divide p(x) by (x + 1):
x3 + 13x2 + 32x + 20 = (x + 1)(x2 + 12x + 20).

Split middle term for quadratic: 12 = 10 + 2 and (10)(2) = 20.
x2 + 12x + 20 = (x + 10)(x + 2).
Therefore: (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 10).
questions.markingScheme:
• Finding factor (x + 1): 1 mark
• Quadratic quotient x2 + 12x + 20: 1 mark
• Final factors (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 10): 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Since all coefficients are positive, trial zeroes must be negative.

questions.prompt: Find the area of a triangle whose sides are 9 cm, 12 cm, and 15 cm. Also find the height corresponding to the longest side.
questions.answer:
1. 92 + 122 = 81 + 144 = 225 = 152 ⇒ Right-angled triangle.
Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 9 × 12 = 54 cm2.
(Or using Heron's formula: s = 36/2 = 18; √[18(9)(6)(3)] = 54 cm2).

2. Longest side = 15 cm. Let corresponding altitude be h.
Area = (1/2) × base × h
54 = (1/2) × 15 × h
15h = 108 ⇒ h = 108 / 15 = 7.2 cm.
questions.markingScheme:
• Calculating Area = 54 cm2: 1.5 marks
• Setting (1/2) × 15 × h = 54 and solving h = 7.2 cm: 1.5 marks
questions.examinerTip: Remember that altitude to hypotenuse is (a × b) / c.

questions.prompt: Prove that: (a + b + c)<sup>3</sup> - a<sup>3</sup> - b<sup>3</sup> - c<sup>3</sup> = 3(a + b)(b + c)(c + a).
questions.answer:
Group terms: (a + b + c) = [(a + b) + c].
LHS = [(a + b) + c]3 - a3 - b3 - c3
= (a + b)3 + c3 + 3(a + b)c[(a + b) + c] - a3 - b3 - c3
= [a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)] + c3 + 3(a + b)c(a + b + c) - a3 - b3 - c3
= 3ab(a + b) + 3(a + b)c(a + b + c)
= 3(a + b) [ ab + c(a + b + c) ]
= 3(a + b) [ ab + ca + bc + c2 ]
= 3(a + b) [ a(b + c) + c(b + c) ]
= 3(a + b)(b + c)(c + a) = RHS. (Hence Proved).
questions.markingScheme:
• Expanding [(a+b) + c]3: 1.5 marks
• Factoring out 3(a+b): 1 mark
• Completing factorization to 3(a+b)(b+c)(c+a): 0.5 mark

questions.prompt: The perimeter of a right triangle is 60 cm and its hypotenuse is 25 cm. Find the area of the triangle and the other two side lengths using algebraic identities and Heron's formula.
questions.answer:
Let the two legs be a and b, and hypotenuse c = 25 cm.

1. Perimeter = a + b + c = 60 ⇒ a + b + 25 = 60 ⇒ a + b = 35 cm.
2. By Pythagoras theorem: a2 + b2 = c2 = 252 = 625.

3. Use identity (a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab:
352 = 625 + 2ab
1225 = 625 + 2ab ⇒ 2ab = 1225 - 625 = 600 ⇒ ab = 300.

4. Area of right triangle = (1/2)ab = (1/2)(300) = 150 cm2.

5. Find sides a and b:
(a - b)2 = (a + b)2 - 4ab = 352 - 4(300) = 1225 - 1200 = 25.
a - b = √25 = 5 cm.
Adding (a + b = 35) and (a - b = 5): 2a = 40 ⇒ a = 20 cm and b = 15 cm.
The sides are 15 cm, 20 cm, and 25 cm, and Area = 150 cm2.
questions.markingScheme:
• a + b = 35 and a2 + b2 = 625: 1.5 marks
• Using identity to get 2ab = 600 ⇒ Area = 150 cm2: 1.5 marks
• Finding (a - b) = 5 and solving sides 15 cm and 20 cm: 2 marks
questions.examinerTip: Connecting geometry with algebraic identities is a favorite CBSE question pattern.

questions.prompt: Find the area of a quadrilateral ABCD in which AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, CD = 4 cm, DA = 5 cm, and AC = 5 cm.
questions.answer:
Divide quadrilateral ABCD into two triangles along diagonal AC: ΔABC and ΔACD.

1. In ΔABC: Sides are AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, AC = 5 cm.
Notice: 32 + 42 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 52 ⇒ ΔABC is a right triangle at B.
Area(ΔABC) = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 3 × 4 = 6 cm2.

2. In ΔACD: Sides are AC = 5 cm, CD = 4 cm, DA = 5 cm.
Semi-perimeter s = (5 + 4 + 5)/2 = 14/2 = 7 cm.
Area(ΔACD) = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)] = √[7(7 - 5)(7 - 4)(7 - 5)]
= √[7 × 2 × 3 × 2] = √[4 × 21] = 2√21 cm2.
Since √21 ≈ 4.583, Area(ΔACD) ≈ 2 × 4.583 ≈ 9.17 cm2.

3. Total Area of quadrilateral ABCD = Area(ΔABC) + Area(ΔACD)
= 6 + 2√21 ≈ 6 + 9.17 = 15.17 cm2.
questions.markingScheme:
• Proving ΔABC is right-angled and finding Area = 6 cm2: 2 marks
• Finding Area(ΔACD) = 2√21 cm2 (≈ 9.17 cm2) via Heron's: 2 marks
• Adding areas to obtain 6 + 2√21 cm2 (approx 15.17 cm2): 1 mark

questions.prompt: If both (x - 2) and (x - 1/2) are factors of px<sup>2</sup> + 5x + r, prove that p = r. Also find the values of p and r.
questions.answer:
Let f(x) = px2 + 5x + r.

1. Since (x - 2) is a factor, f(2) = 0:
p(2)2 + 5(2) + r = 0
4p + 10 + r = 0 ⇒ 4p + r = -10 --- (1)

2. Since (x - 1/2) is a factor, f(1/2) = 0:
p(1/2)2 + 5(1/2) + r = 0
p/4 + 5/2 + r = 0
Multiply by 4:
p + 10 + 4r = 0 ⇒ p + 4r = -10 --- (2)

3. Equating (1) and (2):
4p + r = p + 4r
4p - p = 4r - r
3p = 3r ⇒ p = r. (Hence Proved).

4. Substitute p = r into (1):
4p + p = -10 ⇒ 5p = -10 ⇒ p = -2.
Since p = r, r = -2.
questions.markingScheme:
• Setting up f(2) = 0 ⇒ 4p + r = -10: 1.5 marks
• Setting up f(1/2) = 0 ⇒ p + 4r = -10: 1.5 marks
• Equating to prove p = r: 1 mark
• Solving p = -2, r = -2: 1 mark

questions.prompt:
A highway authority constructed an overpass with triangular side support panels. The dimensions of one triangular concrete wall are 13 m, 14 m, and 15 m. A commercial advertising agency rented the wall surface at ₹ 5,000 per m2 per annum.

Questions:
(i) What is the semi-perimeter of the triangular wall? (1m)
(ii) Find the surface area of the wall using Heron's formula. (2m)
(iii) Calculate the rental revenue generated if the agency rents the wall for 6 months. (1m)
questions.answer:
(i) s = (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 42/2 = 21 m.

(ii) Area = √[21(21 - 13)(21 - 14)(21 - 15)] = √[21 × 8 × 7 × 6]
= √[(7 × 3) × (23) × 7 × (2 × 3)] = √[72 × 32 × 24] = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 m2.

(iii) Annual rent = 84 × ₹ 5,000 = ₹ 4,20,000.
Rent for 6 months = ₹ 4,20,000 × (6/12) = ₹ 2,10,000.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) s = 21 m: 1 mark
• (ii) Area = 84 m2 via Heron's: 2 marks
• (iii) Revenue for 6 months = ₹ 2,10,000: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Directly adapted from School Exam PA-2 Q27.

questions.prompt:
During a geometry lab activity, students plotted three points representing landmark trees on an aerial survey grid: P(2, 3), Q(-2, 3), and R(0, -1).

Questions:
(i) Name the quadrants in which points P and Q lie. (1m)
(ii) On which axis does point R lie? (1m)
(iii) Calculate the length of segment PQ and find the area of ΔPQR. (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) P(2, 3) lies in Quadrant I (+, +). Q(-2, 3) lies in Quadrant II (-, +).

(ii) Point R(0, -1) has abscissa x = 0, so it lies on the negative y-axis.

(iii) Line segment PQ is horizontal along y = 3.
Length PQ = |2 - (-2)| = 2 + 2 = 4 units.
The altitude of ΔPQR is the vertical distance from horizontal line y = 3 down to point R(0, -1):
Height h = 3 - (-1) = 4 units.
Area(ΔPQR) = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 4 × 4 = 8 sq. units.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Quadrants I and II: 1 mark
• (ii) Negative y-axis: 1 mark
• (iii) PQ = 4 units (1 mark) and Area = 8 sq. units (1 mark): 2 marks
questions.examinerTip: Notice that base PQ is horizontal, making height direct vertical subtraction.

questions.prompt:
A science student measures the decay rates of radioactive isotopes in an experiment where decay fractions follow geometric exponent rules:
• The initial mass ratio is modeled as M = (1/2)-3 × (1/4)2.

Questions:
(i) Express (1/2)-3 as a simple integer. (1m)
(ii) Evaluate the mass ratio M in fractional form. (1m)
(iii) If the ratio after time t is given by R(t) = (8)t/3 × (16)-t/4, simplify R(t) into a single power of 2 and find its value when t = 2. (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) (1/2)-3 = 23 = 8.

(ii) M = 8 × (1/4)2 = 8 × (1/16) = 8/16 = 1/2.

(iii) Write 8 and 16 as powers of 2:
8 = 23 ⇒ (8)t/3 = (23)t/3 = 2t.
16 = 24 ⇒ (16)-t/4 = (24)-t/4 = 2-t.
R(t) = 2t × 2-t = 2t - t = 20 = 1.
For any t (including t = 2), R(2) = 1.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) 8: 1 mark
• (ii) M = 1/2: 1 mark
• (iii) Simplifying to 20 = 1: 2 marks
questions.examinerTip: Laws of exponents: 2^t × 2^(-t) = 2^0 = 1 for all t.
